authority-and-trust.law: Application behavior must carry requester, decision, policy and effect-authority references while authority remains owned by the relevant security, product or vertical context.

compatibility-and-evolution.law: Every public contract and behavior edition requires a directional compatibility relation; a successful structural transform is not semantic equivalence.

composition-algebra.law: Composition is an explicitly owned graph of typed requirements/offers, refusals and loss; orchestration does not transfer imported semantic authority.

effect-boundary.law: Decision, authorization, intent, handoff, execution observation and accepted business outcome remain separate stages.

evidence-and-conformance.law: Receipts are scoped observations with provenance and residuals; they are not truth, independent assurance, qualification or business acceptance.

grain-and-cardinality.law: Command, aggregate transition, event occurrence, workflow instance, projection cut, effect attempt and receipt each retain their own identity and cardinality.

identity-and-equality.law: Transport, request, aggregate, event, workflow, effect and attempt identifiers are scoped carriers; equal bytes or names do not imply equal business subjects.

order-and-topology.law: Causation, correlation, workflow control flow, event order, projection checkpoints and effect-attempt order are distinct partial orders; no global total order is inferred.

partiality-and-uncertainty.law: Unknown, partial, duplicate, conflicted, stale, timeout and unobserved outcomes remain explicit and cannot default to success or failure.

privacy-security-safety.law: Purpose, authorization, disclosure, retention, isolation and hazard obligations are imported per operation/effect and never inferred from interface or workflow validity.

representation.law: Schema, API description, event envelope, process notation, state notation and evidence serialization are representations with explicit editions, not the represented business meaning.

resources-and-failure.law: Payload, recursion, retry, deadline, cancellation, concurrency and retention budgets are finite; all operations expose typed refusal and unknown-outcome behavior.

semantic-object.law: Commands, queries, aggregate states/transitions, events, workflows, projections, effect intents/receipts and execution receipts remain distinct semantic objects.

semantic-role.law: Requester, decider, state owner, publisher, coordinator, reader, authorizer, executor, observer and appraiser remain separable roles.

state-and-change.law: Requested, decided, committed, published, coordinated, projected, submitted, observed, reconciled and accepted states are separate lifecycle facts.

time.law: Declaration, validity/effectivity, occurrence, execution, recording, observation, deadline, expiry and reconciliation times remain distinct.

bounded_decision: The complete 16-axis application-behavior applicability candidate is research-resolved for all eight current libraries: every axis is either required or explicitly conditional/imported, with typed non-collapse laws. Four family-level evidence quotients for grain/cardinality, state/change, order/topology and composition/algebra are also research-resolved by the same exact corpus. These are proposed applicability decisions only; named owners must still ratify each member-axis cell.
counterexample_or_negative_twin: A schema-valid idempotent HTTP request can be unauthorized, race an aggregate version, emit a duplicated event, time out after an irreversible effect and leave only a partial receipt.
A well-formed workflow can have bounded retries and a compensation path while the compensation cannot restore disclosed information, shipped goods or an external market action.
Two byte-equal envelopes or receipts can refer to different business subjects, authority scopes, time cuts or attempts.
invalidation_condition: Reopen an axis quotient if a primary specification changes a bounded semantic contract, a member library cannot preserve the stated non-collapse law, a counterexample defeats a candidate disposition, or a named owner changes the family/member scope.
rejected_inferences: family evidence implies every member-axis applicability
structural schema equality implies semantic equality
workflow order implies global event order
application composition owns imported data, runtime, security or vertical semantics

bounded_decision: Adopt the eight current application-behavior library contracts as exact proposed-unratified contract candidates, not as implementations: interaction contracts; aggregate transitions; workflow/saga coordination; event publication; projection/read models; effect handoff; execution evidence; and assembly. Each contract fixes its public types, operations, owner context, imported authorities, configuration points, time roles, finite-resource assumptions, refusal surface, side-effect boundary and compatibility laws. A later ratifier may accept, split, narrow or reject each independently; no provider, portability or vertical acceptance follows.

contract_dispositions.non_collapse: command/query semantics != HTTP or schema representation
query != projection and projection != source authority
decision != authorization != effect intent != execution != outcome
composition imports authority and never transfers it

counterexample_or_negative_twin: Collapsing command validation, aggregate mutation, event publication and effect execution into one library makes a transport retry indistinguishable from a new business decision.
Collapsing projection and query semantics makes a derived stale read model appear to be authoritative source state.
Collapsing execution evidence with outcome acceptance lets a producer attest its own correctness without independent appraisal.
invalidation_condition: Reopen if a contract cannot preserve its exact non-collapse laws, imported authority, total refusal surface, finite-resource semantics or independent lowering boundary, or if named owners provide stronger evidence for splitting or rehoming it.
rejected_inferences: exact proposed contract implies ratified public API
structural test vector implies executed conformance
library graph implies product completeness or vertical acceptance

bounded_decision: The seven residual symbol batches are research-resolved at the classification layer by existing digest-bound P1 archetype programs and exact occurrence candidates. PolicySet, ResourceScope and RetentionRule are distinct policy composition, applicability-scope and lifecycle-rule roles; ForecastOrigin and ForecastHorizon are distinct information-cut and target-offset coordinates; DispositionDue and EventTime are distinct derived eligibility and claimed occurrence positions; DocumentView is a provenance-bound derived representation; AttributeBag is a typed policy-request multiset rather than policy or decision; ResourceBudget is a finite declared vector rather than a physical reservation; application StateTransition is an edition-bound transition record rather than persistence commit. Every shared-owner/import disposition remains proposed and independently owner-ratified migration is still required.
counterexample_or_negative_twin: A retention rule and its calculated disposition-due instant can share fields while having different identity, lifecycle and authority.
A forecast origin and forecast horizon can both be time-shaped while one fixes the information cut and the other fixes target offsets.
A ResourceBudget value can bound an analysis without reserving CPU, memory, queue capacity or cost.
A DocumentView can be reproducible from one rendition yet differ from the source document and from a view produced by another OCR/layout edition.
An application state transition can be accepted by pure logic while its persistence commit conflicts or remains unobserved.
invalidation_condition: Reopen a batch if an exact occurrence, definition digest, archetype source set, candidate semantic position, negative twin or named-owner disposition changes, or if independent review demonstrates a homonym requiring qualification or rename.
rejected_inferences: identical placeholder digest implies semantic equality
same carrier shape implies shared owner
time-shaped value implies same time role
